narrative:
FY2026 budget operating income is £194.3M, +11.9% on FY2025 actuals of £173.6M. The 9+3 forecast stands at £187.8M — £6.5M below budget — even though the loan book is £5.18Bn, 4% ahead of plan.

The gap is margin, not volume. Two Bank Rate cuts repriced about £2.0Bn of bridging, development and wholesale loans within a month, while £2.35Bn of fixed-term bonds keep their 4.85% rate until maturity. Specialist Mortgages (−£4.9M) and Savings & Treasury (−£1.8M) carry the miss; Bridging is £0.5M ahead on completions of £58M a month.

Key risk: one more 25 bp cut in December would take another £1.5M out of FY2026 NII unless deposit pricing follows.
